s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive skin condition with itchy eruptions, nodules, and lymphadenopathy
salient_findings: Extensive, dry scaly patches on the trunk, arms, and legs
Dome-shaped, red papules and nodules on the upper back
Mildly enlarged lymph nodes in the cervical, axillary, and inguinal regions
key_facts: 12-year history of itchy eruptions over the whole body
Nodules appeared on the upper back 1 year previously and gradually increased in number and size
Patient denied a family history of inherited ichthyosis or atopy
Physical examination revealed extensive, dry scaly patches on the trunk, arms, and legs
Several 0.5- to 1-cm, dome-shaped, red papules and nodules were found on the upper back
Mildly enlarged lymph nodes were observed on the cervical, axillary, and inguinal regions
Routine blood tests, biochemistry analyses, and peripheral blood flow cytometry tests were within normal limits
DNA analysis from paraffin sections showed clonal amplification product for the γ-chain of the T-cell receptor
Biopsy from back nodules showed atrophy of the epidermis with focal orthokeratosis and extensive, dense infiltrate of lymphocytes in the entire dermis

shortlist.label: Mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, progressive skin condition with itchy eruptions, nodules, and lymphadenopathy, consistent with clinical and histopathologic findings

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Clonal amplification product for the γ-chain of the T-cell receptor and atypical lymphocytes with epidermotropism support this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Sézary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of itchy eruptions, nodules, and lymphadenopathy, along with clonal T-cell population, makes this a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Granulomatous slack skin disease
shortlist.why_kept: Extensive, dense infiltrate of lymphocytes in the dermis and atrophy of the epidermis are consistent with this rare condition

shortlist.label: Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lymphadenopathy and presence of atypical lymphocytes with focal areas of epidermotropism make this a possible, though less common, diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's 12-year history of itchy eruptions, presence of dome-shaped nodules on the upper back, and histopathology showing atrophy of the epidermis with focal orthokeratosis and extensive, dense infiltrate of lymphocytes in the entire dermis, along with immunohistochemical staining positive for CD2, CD3, CD4, and CD45RO, are consistent with Mycosis fungoides, a type of Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Sézary syndrome
rejected.why: Sézary syndrome typically presents with more systemic involvement, including atypical cells in the peripheral blood, which were not found in this patient.

rejected.label: Granulomatous slack skin disease
rejected.why: Granulomatous slack skin disease is characterized by granulomatous infiltrates and elastolysis, which were not described in the histopathology results.

rejected.label: Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma typically involves the subcutaneous tissue, which was not the primary site of involvement in this patient.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: While Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma is a broader category that includes Mycosis fungoides, the specific features of this patient's presentation are more consistent with Mycosis fungoides, making it a more specific and appropriate diagnosis.
